subject: Landing zone handover: network egress controls, CSI profiles, and node lifecycle
messages:
From: Jack Smith <jack.smith@landlord.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.example.com>
Cc: ops-team@landlord.io
Date: 2026-05-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private cluster: acceptance criteria & final handover

Hi Markus / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We need a concise acceptance checklist to share with our ops/infra team before we cut over the first tenant. Key items we care about: egress controls through our NAT/BGP pair, validated StorageClass profiles (CSI driver compatibility with snapshots), and a short node lifecycle policy (eviction, drain, reprovision cadence). Can you send a single consolidated doc and call out any gating items that require our network or security approvals?

One constraint: our datacenter enforces MTU=9000 on the physical fabric — anything needed on your side to support jumbo frames?

Appreciate it,
Jack
Jack Smith
Head of Infrastructure, Landlord Health
ops-team@landlord.io

Attachments: none
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.example.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-05-09T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster: acceptance criteria & final handover

Hi Jack — thanks, clear list. I’ve attached a compact acceptance checklist (landingzone-acceptance-checklist.pdf) and a sample CSI StorageClass YAML we typically provision for block-store volumes. High level notes up front: 

- Network / egress: Redwood’s private deployment supports both routed peering (BGP) and VPC-like NAT egressing. For your setup we recommend BGP peer to one of our edge routers and a secondary NAT gateway as an emergency path. We will need the ASN and the /29 you want routed to us; if you want asymmetric egress via your NAT, we’ll need a firewall rule to allow outbound to our control plane IPs (listed in the checklist).

- MTU: we support MTU=9000 end-to-end but require the host OS kubelet + CNI MTU setting to match. If your ToR has offload, we’ll test with a 1G/10G jumbo frame profile in staging first.

- Storage / CSI: the provided sample StorageClass uses the in-cluster CSI driver with snapshotClass enabled; we recommend enabling volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer for tenant PVCs. Our backup operator takes consistent snapshots and uploads to the object-store endpoint you nominate. Snapshot retention is configurable — we outlined a default 7-day rolling retention in the checklist.

- Node lifecycle: recommend three nodepools: control-plane (managed by Redwood, pinned), worker-standard (cpu/memory mix, autoscale 3-30), and worker-storage (nodes with local NVMe for cache workloads). Eviction policy: kubelet evictionThresholds tuned to leave 500Mi system reserve; we will run a drain with NodeCondition taints before reprovision. We’ve included a short runbook for emergency reprovision in the checklist.

I’ve attached the checklist and the sample csi-storageclass-samples.yaml. Next step: can your Ops sign off on Sections 2 (BGP + NAT) and 4 (MTU) by EOD Tuesday? After sign-off we’ll schedule the final staging run.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Account Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: landingzone-acceptance-checklist.pdf (type: application/pdf), csi-storageclass-samples.yaml (type: text/yaml)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>

Date: 2026-05-10T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster: acceptance criteria & final handover

Jack — adding a few storage-specific clarifications from the ops side: 

1) StorageClass variants: we included two StorageClasses in the YAML: fast-ssd (reclaimPolicy: Delete, fsType: xfs, volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer) and durable-block (reclaimPolicy: Retain, fsType: ext4). For tenant databases we recommend durable-block + regular snapshot schedule.

2) CSI snapshot testing: we will create test PVC -> snapshot -> restore in your staging namespace. This validates the snapshotClass and our snapshot-controller RBAC against your object store credentials. Please provision an object-store temp creds with write/list access.

3) Local NVMe caching: worker-storage pool will have a hostPath-backed cache for hot tokens/embeddings; we will not put user data on local NVMe unless you explicitly opt in. Backups still go to object-store.

4) Encryption: we support provider-managed KMS or customer KMS (preferred for regulated data). If you choose customer KMS, we need KMS endpoint + access policy prior to cutover.

I’ve added a short snippet to the YAML for snapshotClass and included test steps in the checklist. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through snapshots live.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior PM, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Jack — quick confirmation from my side before we lock dates: 

- BGP peering: Redwood can peer to your existing edges; no dedicated route-target required. We do ask for a /29 for control-plane reachability (temporary for the staging window) and an agreed set of community tags for failover.

- Object store: any bucket prefixed landlord-redwood-<env> works. Temporary write/list creds for staging are fine; production will require scoped service principal + rotating keys (we can provide a template IAM policy).

- MTU: confirm that staging ToR is configured for 9000 and we’ll run a throughput probe in staging to validate no fragmentation.

Next steps: once Jack’s team signs sections 2 and 4 in the attached checklist, Markus / Neha will schedule a 3-hour staging window next week. I’ll approve blackout windows with support and send a shared calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to finishing this out.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference
